 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jellyfish:-**

 
 
• These are gelatinous marine animals with umbrella-shaped bells and trailing tentacles.
 
• They are members of the phylum Cnidaria, which also includes corals, sea anemones, and hydras.
 
• Jellyfish are found in all of the world's oceans, from the surface to the deep sea. 
 
• **Jellyfish are coelenterates. **
 
• Coelenterates are a phylum of aquatic animals that are characterized by their radially symmetrical bodies, two layers of cells (ectoderm and endoderm), and a gastrovascular cavity (coelenteron).
 
 
 
• **Crayfish**:-
 
 
• It is also known as crawfish, crawdads, mudbugs, or freshwater lobsters, are aquatic crustaceans that live in freshwater habitats such as rivers, streams, lakes, and ponds.
 
• **It belongs to the arthropoda phlyum.**
 
• They are found all over the world except for Antarctica, and there are over 500 species of crayfish known to science. 
 
 
 
• **Whalefish:-**
 
 
• **They are a family of deep-sea fish that are related to anglerfish and barbeled dragonfish and belongs to mammal.**
 
• They are named for their resemblance to whales, with large heads, gaping mouths, and streamlined bodies.
 
• Whalefish are found in all the world's oceans, at depths of up to 3,000 meters.
 
 
 
• **Devilfish**:-
 
 
• The devilfish, also known as the giant Pacific octopus, is a cephalopod mollusk native to the northern Pacific Ocean.
 
• **Devil fish belongs to Mollusca.**
 
• It is the largest octopus species in the world, with females growing up to 15 meters (50 feet) in arm span and weighing up to 50 kilograms (110 pounds).
